checkpoints.description: [1/3] Rebuild a devastated inhabited world in the current system

impact_assessment.why: /api/reconstruct stays context claiming it needs a devastated world in orbit, but a 2,000-step campaign shows 55 devastated inhabited worlds across the galaxy after the wars and the snapshot carries population and devastation for every current-system body; the captain never orbits one, so the war-recovery mechanic and its standing gain have no AI proof
impact_assessment.benefits: Whenever the current system holds a devastated inhabited world the captain orbits the worst one and funds a 600 cr reconstruction, reducing devastation and earning standing; the route is exercised during campaigns without touching the short gate, which predates the war declarations
impact_assessment.risks: contract: /api/reconstruct joins SIGNATURE_ROUTES keyed by body_id and keeps a narrowed CONTEXT_ACTIONS reason for the short gate (additive); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: 600 credits, 20 devastation points and standing through the existing engine path
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the orbit, reconstruct, landed, no-target, credit and one-shot rules, a drift test for the cost mirror, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42, full suite and 5/5 gates

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Prospect a derelict and scoop fuel after the campaign

impact_assessment.why: /api/salvage and /api/scoop are attempted in campaigns but never succeed because the captain tries both at whatever body it happens to orbit (usually a station science body) where there is no derelict and no accessible volatiles; the derelict and scoop mechanics have no successful AI proof and post-story ships end seeds on fumes (seed 1 fuel 6/80)
impact_assessment.benefits: After Act VI the captain probes one plausible derelict body and orbits a scoopable body when the tank is low, so salvage and fuel scooping succeed for real cargo, credits and fuel instead of refused attempts
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no route or signature change, two state-driven post-story actions only and the 180 gate is untouched by the completed-story gate; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one claimed derelict and a refuelled tank through the existing engine paths
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for candidate filtering, the probe limit, the low-fuel gate, the scoopable-body choice and the post-story gate, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Recall the armed escort and spend its captain's gambit in a fight

impact_assessment.why: /api/combat/gambit stays context claiming it needs an active fight and a local escort captain, but a 2,000-step seed-1 campaign has both a crewed escort and one pirate intercept; they never line up because the patrol rotation stations the escort on a connected lane while the fight breaks out in the current system, so the once-per-battle gambit has no AI proof
impact_assessment.benefits: A fight with an armed escort anywhere in the fleet recalls that escort into the current system and spends the role-appropriate gambit once, so the combat command is exercised for real
impact_assessment.risks: contract: /api/combat/gambit keeps a narrowed CONTEXT_ACTIONS reason and gains no signature entry because it is one-shot per campaign; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one escort reassignment and one spent gambit through the existing engine paths
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the ready local gambit, recall-first path, one-recall cap, spent-battle and one-shot guards, unarmed-escort skip and role gates, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Switch the reactor doctrine once after the campaign

impact_assessment.why: /api/reactor/mode is attempted in every campaign but always refused because the rotating tour reposts the current balanced mode; the four-mode doctrine has no successful AI proof, and switching during the 180-step gate reroutes the trip (57 families/62 attempted/8 gaps)
impact_assessment.benefits: A post-Act-VI captain moves the core to economy once, proving the doctrine change and its heat/output trade-off without disturbing the short gate
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the tour keeps its legacy behavior and a new one-shot post-story action owns the change; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: reactor mode switched to economy through the existing engine path
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the economy-first choice, balanced fallback, legacy list catalog, single-mode and missing-catalog skips, pre-campaign gate and one-shot rule, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Run a contraband lot at the quoted customs cordon

impact_assessment.why: /api/customs/resolve stayed context as prompt-driven: a scan only rolls on arrival in a security-0.65+ system with contraband held, and ordinary play almost never paired those; the snapshot quoted the cordon's name and chance but not its id, so a deliberate run could not aim at it
impact_assessment.benefits: After the campaign the captain buys one contraband lot, ferries the quoted cordon until the scan fires and dumps the lot under pressure, proving the smuggling loop and its evasion stat without touching the short gate
impact_assessment.risks: contract: customs_risk_status gains one additive system_id field and no route signature changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one contraband lot bought, ferried and jettisoned through the existing engine paths
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first engine assertion for the id plus ten agent tests for the purchase, cordon jump, refuel guard, reposition hop, jump cap and one-shot/lost-lot guards, 180-step gate measurement, 2,000-step campaigns on seeds 1/2/42 plus seed 7, full suite and project gates

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Rotate the post-story fallback jump across the affordable lanes

impact_assessment.why: affordable[step % len(affordable)] froze on one slot because the twenty-step cadence repeats the remainder, so the captain ping-ponged between two systems and the megastructure policy never probed a restorable world on seed 2
impact_assessment.benefits: Post-story exploration visits every affordable lane, recovering late-game mechanics that the shuttle silently starved, while the pre-story route that the 180 gate was measured on stays frozen
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, the jump route and body are unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: a rotation counter only
impact_assessment.mitigation: five agent tests for rotation, preserved first slot, pre-story freeze, affordability and cadence plus the 180-step gate and three campaign seeds
